article_title: Evaluating fluid and crystallized abilities in the performance of an educational process
citation: Angel Blanch. (2015). Evaluating fluid and crystallized abilities in the performance of an educational process. Springer Verlag. http://hdl.handle.net/10459.1/48328
title: Gf–Gc investment theory: fluid ability drives the rate of learning and feeds crystallized ability, which determines attained performance levels
description: The Cattell-Horn fluid–crystallized theory distinguishes Gf, the basic processes for resolving abstract and novel problems, from Gc, knowledge acquired through culturally transmitted language, information, and concepts. Its dynamic predictions propose that "the investment of Gf influences the course of Gc and educational outcomes during the schooling period." The article tests three investment predictions — Gf influencing Gc but not vice versa, Gc growth starting beyond a point in Gf development, and faster growth for Gf-related processes — against learning growth factors from a brief instructional intervention, finding the interplay of both factors more important for learning than either alone.
requirements: Assessment of both broad Gf and Gc factors prior to or alongside the learning process being explained
constraints: The article notes the ninth property could only be partially assessed because the dataset contained no information on educational performance in already studied areas
No data were available about motivation, interests, personality, or situational factors such as parental involvement
target_learning_goals: Acquisition of novel concepts and procedures in a structured instructional unit sequence
examples: The study evaluated the theory against a one-week instructional project on the imaginary science Xenograde Systems using a latent curve model with intercept and slope growth factors
key_sources: Angel Blanch. (2015). Evaluating fluid and crystallized abilities in the performance of an educational process. Springer Verlag. http://hdl.handle.net/10459.1/48328
